title: Prevent whole-note duplication across sync cold starts and reconnects
description: The staging note u9gn7tgwsz2g persisted its entire 22-block document twice, including the table and attachment. Decoding description_state shows two independent Yjs clients (2820699682 and 3490987223), each with the same 155 structs/283 clocks and the same 22 top-level nodes; a third client only contributed six clocks. A focused local reproduction confirms that merging two independent TiptapTransformer.toYdoc conversions of the same HTML yields duplicated paragraphs and tables. The note remained schema version 9 and was last stored at 2026-08-26T03:49:09Z, shortly after the legacy campsite-sync-tokdio container restarted at 03:43:32Z/declared ready at 03:45:01Z. The sync design converts description_html to a fresh Y.Doc whenever description_state is absent, but has no atomic initialization/CAS or distributed document coordination across overlapping instances and reconnecting clients. Diagnose the exact race and make initialization and rolling deploys safe; do not merely delete the duplicate data.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent cold loads of a note with HTML but no Yjs state cannot create two independent base snapshots; two collaborators remain consistent through a sync-server rolling replacement/reconnect; table and attachment content appears once; a regression test reproduces the prior duplicate merge and passes; existing populated Yjs state remains byte/semantic compatible.
notes: Implemented in local history plus final hardening: Hocuspocus providers use autoConnect:false, connect only after auth, and disconnect while connecting; clients no longer preload REST Yjs state; the collaborative editor stays read-only/non-mutating until onSynced. HTML fallback now atomically initializes description_state under a Rails row lock, and concurrent losers receive the winning canonical state. Added a real two-loader transformer regression containing heading, table, attachment, and paragraph. Validation: sync-server 39/39; focused web 8/8; Rails controllers 28 runs/89 assertions; web tsc pass; sync build pass; Prettier/RuboCop/diff checks pass. Standalone sync tsc still has pre-existing facade.ts:214 YXmlHook error. Follow-ups: campsite-vqa.13 for the legacy mention-label job that clears state; campsite-vqa.14 for first-party Redis multi-replica coordination requiring a stewardship dependency exception.
close_reason: The duplicate-root regression is fixed with effect-owned provider lifecycle, server-authoritative first sync, atomic canonical initialization, and table/attachment multi-loader coverage. Remaining distinct mutation and multi-replica concerns are tracked in campsite-vqa.13 and campsite-vqa.14.

title: Diagnose Rails credentials decryption failure

title: [bug] Lambda subdomain constraints broke auth/admin URL generation
description:
Commit aa02b58 (2026-08-24, 'fix(deploy): recognize private auth subdomains') replaced the declarative route constraints 'constraints subdomain: ENV[AUTH_SUBDOMAIN]' and the ADMIN_SUBDOMAIN equivalent with lambda constraints: constraints ->(request) { auth_subdomains.include?(request.subdomain) }.

In production any code calling these helpers emits a URL on the apex host that will not route.
design: Keep multi-subdomain recognition without losing generation. Options: (a) declare the route set once per subdomain with a declarative 'constraints subdomain:' block per entry in AUTH_SUBDOMAINS, (b) keep the lambda for recognition but set the canonical subdomain in default_url_options / an explicit :subdomain on the helpers, or (c) restore the declarative constraint using the first configured subdomain as canonical and match the rest via middleware/host rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: new_integrations_auth_url generates a host carrying the configured auth subdomain; the 17 callback controller tests pass; multi-subdomain recognition from aa02b58 still works.

WORKING SERVICE CONSTRAINTS for this 1-2 user deployment, pending any later operator override:
- RPO: at most 24 hours for durable application data at initial cutover; Redis cache is disposable, but Sidekiq durable jobs require drain/reconciliation.
- RTO: at most 8 hours.

AUDIT CONCLUSION:
Every production component and data source has an identified owner/path. Live data quantities requiring Fly/provider authority are explicitly UNAVAILABLE. Odin is suitable for low-traffic stateless runtimes; Shuri is suitable for capped single-node Elasticsearch. The platform design must account for Asgard host memory pressure, Forge availability, Shuri backup coverage, single-site power risk, and starkdrive capacity.

title: Adopt @tiptap/static-renderer: DOM-free JSON→HTML in styled-text-server + sync-server
description:
Adopt `@tiptap/static-renderer` in styled-text-server (and sync-server) to render PM JSON -> HTML string with NO DOM — removes the JSDOM dependency and becomes the foundation for the Slack/plain-text/markdown projections.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- Package: `@tiptap/static-renderer` ^3.29.2, MIT. Entry: `import { renderToHTMLString } from '@tiptap/static-renderer/pm/html-string'` — takes `{extensions, content}` where extensions = our kits from @campsite/editor; no jsdom, no editor instance. Also has React and markdown targets under other subpaths, and per-node `nodeMapping`/`markMapping` overrides for custom output.
- styled-text-server: apps/styled-text-server/src/markdown.ts currently does markdown -> parsedNode -> DOMSerializer.fromSchema(...).serializeFragment with a JSDOM document. Replace the serialize half with renderToHTMLString(node.toJSON()). JSDOM still needed by the PARSE half (our MarkdownParser uses DOMParser for html blocks) — full JSDOM removal only lands with the parse migration; this bead still deletes the DOMSerializer/JSDOM usage on output and unblocks the other projections.
- sync-server: apps/sync-server/src/database.ts store() uses generateHTML from @tiptap/html — same swap applies; fetch() uses generateJSON (parse direction, keep).
- Suggested structure: export a shared `renderDocumentToHTML(json, editorKind)` from packages/editor so web/sync-server/styled-text-server use ONE renderer.
- moduleResolution note: repo tsconfigs use "node"; subpath imports like `@tiptap/static-renderer/pm/html-string` may need the dist-path workaround used for `@tiptap/react/dist/menus` (see EditorBubbleMenu.tsx) — or works directly in styled-text-server if its tsconfig uses node16/bundler (check apps/styled-text-server/tsconfig.json, it was modernized recently).

title: styled-text-server: rebuild html_to_slack as ProseMirror serialization
description:
Rebuild html_to_slack as a ProseMirror serialization instead of cheerio string surgery: parse HTML into a PM doc with our schema, then map nodes -> Slack blocks explicitly.

**Current code:** apps/styled-text-server/src/html.ts (~179 lines): cheerio + jsx-slack with string-level hacks (br/hr self-closing rewrites, checkbox -> emoji, blockquote heading flattening, 2000-char link stripping, hr -> unicode line). Unknown HTML silently leaks or is stripped.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- Parse: PM DOMParser.fromSchema(schema) over the incoming HTML (schema from @campsite/editor kits) — this alone structurally sanitizes input (only schema-known nodes/marks survive).
- Serialize: walk the doc (or use @tiptap/static-renderer's nodeMapping with a custom target) emitting jsx-slack elements/Block Kit JSON per node type: paragraph->Section, heading->bold Section/Header, bulletList/orderedList/taskItem (checkbox emoji logic moves into the taskItem handler), codeBlock->code fence, blockquote->quote prefix, hr->divider, link (keep the >2000 char guard, now per-mark), mention->@display, image/attachment->context or link.
- Unknown node types: throw/log loudly instead of leaking markup.
- Consumers in api: post/build_slack_blocks.rb, comment/build_slack_blocks.rb, zapier paths — API contract unchanged (same /html_to_slack in+out), so ship behind a comparison test: run old cheerio path vs new path over fixture corpus (existing __tests__ in apps/styled-text-server) and diff.
- Depends on: static-renderer bead (shared renderer infra), not blocked by it strictly.

description:
Add markdown OUTPUT to styled-text-server via the official `@tiptap/markdown` package: html_to_markdown and (once JSON interchange exists) json_to_markdown endpoints. Primary consumers: LLM jobs in api — generate_post_tldr_job.rb, generate_call_recording_summary_section_job.rb, generate_post_resolution_job.rb — which should feed models markdown instead of HTML (fewer tokens, better model behavior).

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- Package: `@tiptap/markdown` 3.29.x/3.30.0, MIT (verified on npm). This is the official v3 markdown system — v3 extensions ship built-in markdown specs (e.g. @tiptap/extension-details dist calls `createBlockMarkdownSpec({nodeName:'details', content:'block'})`).
- Pipeline: HTML -> PM doc (existing schema from getNoteExtensions/ALL_EDITORS in packages/editor) -> markdown string via @tiptap/markdown serializer. No DOM needed for the serialize direction.
- Custom nodes needing explicit markdown serializers (they have no first-party spec): mention, reaction, resourceMention, postNoteAttachment, mediaGallery, linkUnfurl, relativeTime, kbd, comment mark, details (ours is extended). Sensible fallbacks: mentions -> `@username`, reactions -> emoji char, attachments/galleries -> image/link markdown, linkUnfurl -> plain link, relativeTime -> formatted text, comment mark -> drop.
- Keep the EXISTING forked parser (packages/editor/src/utils/MarkdownParser.ts + markdownParseSpec config keys) for the parse direction for now — swapping parse is a separate, riskier migration; serialize-only is additive.

- Tests: round-trip snapshots against packages/editor/src/utils/__tests__/createMarkdownParser.test.ts fixtures.

title: EditorBubbleMenu: replace forceUpdate-on-transaction with useEditorState
description:
Replace the manual force-rerender in EditorBubbleMenu with Tiptap v3's `useEditorState` selector hook.

**Current code:** apps/web/components/EditorBubbleMenu/EditorBubbleMenu.tsx subscribes `editor.on('transaction', forceUpdate)` (via useForceUpdate) to keep `editor.isActive(...)` states fresh — rerenders the whole menu on EVERY transaction.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- `import { useEditorState } from '@tiptap/react'` (already installed).
- Pattern:
  `const s = useEditorState({ editor, selector: ({ editor }) => ({ bold: editor.isActive('bold'), italic: editor.isActive('italic'), ..., linkHref: editor.getAttributes('link').href }) })`
  — equality-checked, so the menu only rerenders when derived state changes.
- Replaces both the `forceUpdate` transaction listener and the `selectionUpdate` -> setUrl effect (fold `getAttributes('link').href` into the selector).
- Note: the editor is created with `shouldRerenderOnTransaction: false` in useNoteEditor — useEditorState is the intended companion.
- Pure perf/cleanliness; no behavior change expected. Verify menu active-state toggling + link editor URL sync manually.

title: sync-server: re-authorize live connections via Hocuspocus 4 onTokenSync
description:
Use Hocuspocus 4's onTokenSync hook in sync-server to re-authorize live note connections without reconnecting.

**Context (researched 2026-08-12, @hocuspocus/server 4.6.0):**
- Today apps/sync-server/src/index.ts only authorizes in onAuthenticate (connect time): fetches sync state from api, sets connectionConfig.readOnly from schemaVersion, returns Context {token, schemaVersion, organization, type}. A revoked membership/token stays live until the socket drops.
- v4 adds `onTokenSync(data: onTokenSyncPayload)` — fires when the provider re-sends a token; payload includes connection + context (see dist/packages/server/src/types.d.ts onTokenSyncPayload: context, document, documentName, requestParameters, connection, connectionConfig...). Re-run the getResource authorization there; on failure throw to drop the connection, or flip connection.readOnly.
- Client side: @hocuspocus/provider 4.6 token option already is a callback returning a fresh token (apps/web useEditorSync postMeSyncToken) — check provider config for token refresh interval/trigger (see provider d.ts) and wire periodic refresh.
- Also consider v4 sessionAwareness (per-tab awareness) — only if we ever multiplex docs on one socket; not needed now.

title: styled-text-server: PM JSON as first-class interchange (json endpoints + structural sanitization)
description:
Make PM JSON a first-class interchange format in styled-text-server: add /markdown_to_json, /html_to_json, /json_to_html, /json_to_text endpoints so api can pass canonical validated documents instead of HTML strings.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- JSON->HTML: renderToHTMLString from @tiptap/static-renderer (see static-renderer bead).
- HTML->JSON: PM DOMParser.fromSchema(schema).parse(dom).toJSON() — needs a DOM for parse; keep JSDOM for this path (or cheerio-free happy-dom). Structural sanitization freebie: only schema-known nodes/marks/attrs survive — stronger than tag allowlists for the untrusted markdown/HTML arriving via api markdown_enrichable.rb and Zapier controllers.
- markdown->JSON: existing createStandaloneMarkdownParser (packages/editor) already produces parsedNode — just return node.toJSON() instead of serializing to HTML.
- JSON->text: static-renderer text extraction (or doc.textBetween) for search indexing / notification previews / OG descriptions — replaces HTML stripping in Rails.
- `editor` param (ALL_EDITORS in packages/editor: note/post/comment/chat kits) selects the schema, mirroring /markdown_to_html.
- Add matching methods to api/lib StyledText client. Version the endpoints or gate by param — Rails deploys decouple from node deploys.

title: styled-text-server: semantic diff endpoint via vendored recreate-transform
description:
Semantic diff endpoint in styled-text-server: given two ProseMirror doc states (JSON or HTML), compute what changed — the primitive for "what changed in this note" notification digests, edit summaries, and feeding only deltas to LLM summarizers.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- We already vendor prosemirror-recreate-transform at packages/editor/src/lib/recreate-transform (recreate.js computes steps between two docs via recreateTransform; merge.js exists too). It is plain JS, editor-agnostic — usable server-side with the schema from packages/editor.
- Endpoint sketch: POST /diff {before, after, editor, format: 'steps'|'summary'} -> recreateTransform(docBefore, docAfter, {complexSteps:true, wordDiffs:true}) -> map ReplaceSteps to human-readable changes (node type + text snippet) or return raw steps.
- Depends on the JSON interchange endpoints bead (docs in, not HTML) for clean input; HTML input possible via schema DOMParser meanwhile.
- Consumers to wire later in api: notification digests, note edit summaries.

title: Evaluate UniqueID extension for stable block IDs (needs NOTE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump)
description:
Add stable block-level IDs to notes via `@tiptap/extension-unique-id` — the primitive for block deep-links, block-anchored comments, and reliable ToC anchors.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12, MIT since Tiptap 3):**
- Package: `@tiptap/extension-unique-id` ^3.29.2 (verified MIT on npm).
- Configure `types: ['heading', 'paragraph', 'codeBlock', ...]` (choose deliberately; every listed type gets a persisted `id` attr) and `attributeName` (default 'id' -> renders `data-id`).
- **BREAKING for persisted docs:** adds attributes to the stored JSON/HTML, so bump `NOTE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (defined in packages/editor, used by apps/web useEditorSync + apps/sync-server onAuthenticate readOnly gate). Old clients get read-only'd until refresh — ship like previous schema bumps.
- Collab caveat: UniqueID must generate IDs deterministically wrt Yjs — the extension handles collab (it was built for it), but test duplicate-ID repair with two concurrent clients on sync-server (Hocuspocus 4.6).
- styled-text-server/round-trip: markdown output/parse will drop ids (fine — regenerate on load); HTML output will carry data-id attrs — confirm api HTML sanitizers keep or strip them consistently.
- Only adopt with a concrete feature behind it (block comments / copy-link-to-block).
design: Adopt only as an exact-version editor-graph migration after the current latest stable clears the repository supply-chain age policy. Configure a deliberately bounded block-node list, use filterTransaction with collaboration-origin detection, and mount the editor only after the Hocuspocus provider has synchronized. Treat the addition as NOTE_SCHEMA_VERSION 11 or later based on the version current at implementation time. Acceptance must cover initial ID backfill, split/merge/paste/undo/redo, duplicate repair across two Hocuspocus clients, stale-client read-only enforcement, agent-facade writes, HTML/Markdown/rendering behavior, and the concrete Copy link to block action.
notes: Revalidated 2026-08-26. Official source is npm @tiptap/extension-unique-id from github.com/ueberdosis/tiptap/packages/extension-unique-id, MIT. Registry latest is 3.30.3, published 2026-08-24T03:23:11Z; exact peers are @tiptap/core 3.30.3 and @tiptap/pm 3.30.3, dependency uuid ^14.0.0. Campsite currently pins the complete Tiptap graph to 3.30.1 and already resolves uuid 14.0.1, so standalone installation would violate exact peers. minimumReleaseAge is strict seven days; earliest eligible time is 2026-08-31T03:23:11Z, subject to rechecking latest stable and changelog then. NOTE_SCHEMA_VERSION is already 10, so the old planned bump to 10 is stale. Critical integration gap: useEditorSync constructs/connects the provider immediately and useNoteEditor mounts whenever provider exists; official docs require waiting for provider sync before mounting UniqueID or it can preserve unintended empty state. No dependency, lockfile, schema, or runtime change was made in this preparation pass.

title: Refactor editor consumers for deferred SSR mounting
description: The current note, Markdown, and chat editor consumers dereference the result of useEditor synchronously. Tiptap v3's immediatelyRender: false makes that result nullable until client initialization, so adopt guarded rendering and then enable deferred SSR-safe initialization before considering manual mount/unmount reuse.
design: Keep each editor's content and collaboration provider ownership local. Do not reuse one instance across notes/posts; validate hydration, focus, attachments, comments, and collaboration lifecycle before changing editor mount behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All editor consumers safely handle a null initial editor; immediatelyRender: false is enabled where SSR applies; hydration and focused editor interactions pass; no stale content or collaboration providers survive a remount.

title: Evaluate FileHandler extension vs custom paste/drop upload plumbing
description:
Evaluate replacing the custom paste/drop upload plumbing with `@tiptap/extension-file-handler` (free/MIT since Tiptap 3).

**Current code:** apps/web/components/MarkdownEditor/useEditorFileHandlers.ts (~114 lines) implements editorProps handlePaste/handleDrop wired into useUploadAttachments; notes use apps/web/components/Post/Notes/Attachments/useUploadAttachments.ts.

**Integration details (researched 2026-08-12):**
- Package: `@tiptap/extension-file-handler` ^3.29.2. Config: `onDrop(editor, files, pos)`, `onPaste(editor, files, htmlContent)`, `allowedMimeTypes`.
- Would replace the editorProps handlers with extension config, keeping our upload pipeline (optimistic attachment nodes via insertAttachments command in packages/editor PostNoteAttachment).
- Gotcha: onPaste gives you `htmlContent` when the clipboard has both HTML and files — our current handler has ordering logic for that case (e.g. pasting an image copied from a browser); port it carefully.
- Low urgency: current code is thin and battle-tested. Do it opportunistically when next touching upload UX.
